title: Stock Market Today Live, Aug 19: Sensex slips 150 pts, Nifty below 24,100 as bond yield spike rattle markets; Brent crude climbs toward $92 - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Sensex Today, Nifty 50 | Stock Market Live Updates - Find here all the live updates related to Sensex, Nifty, BSE, NSE, share prices and Indian stock markets for 19th August 2026.

The Nifty 50 opened at 24,152.05, against its previous close of 24,154.90, and was trading at 24,114.00, down 40.90 points or 0.17 per cent, as of 9.17 AM. The Sensex opened at 77,218.05 against its previous close of 77,235.46, and was quoting at 77,127.18, down 108.28 points or 0.14 per cent.

The 30-year U.S. Treasury yield has climbed to its highest level since 2007, approaching 5.33 per cent–5.34 per cent intraday, driven by widening fiscal deficits, inflation concerns, and heavy capital demand from debt-financed AI infrastructure. Bond yields are also rising in Japan, where the 10-year government bond yield is approaching 3 per cent, a three-decade high, and in Germany, adding to the global pressure on equities.

Brent climbed toward $92 a barrel, after adding 4.5% over the previous three sessions, while West Texas Intermediate was near $86. US President Donald Trump insisted Tuesday that there were no talks ongoing with Tehran.

The rupee weakened 8 paise to close at ₹95.68 per dollar on Tuesday, pressured by higher crude prices and weak domestic equities.

Nifty 50 August Futures contract can fall to 23,980. But thereafter a bounce back move is possible

Shares traded at 315.35, up 6.20 points or 2.01% at NSE

Panorama Studios has made an undisclosed investment in Rocket Reels, an original-stories vertical OTT platform, at a valuation of Rs 200 crore, the company said on Tuesday.

The investment underscores the growing confidence in the future of premium short-form storytelling and positions Rocket Reels for its next phase of growth, innovation, and global expansion, a statement said, without revealing the stake or the size of the investment. (PTI)

Brent crude futures climbed 69 cents, or 0.8%, to $91.71 by 0415 GMT, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude futures were up 76 cents, ‌or 0.9%, to $85.70 a barrel.

Both contracts closed on Tuesday at their highest in more than three weeks as hopes of peace ‌between the U.S. and Iran faded.

Temasek-backed e-commerce logistics services ‌firm Shiprocket jumped ⁠35.1% in debut trade on ‌Wednesday, after ‌robust ‌investor ⁠response to ⁠its $170 million initial public offering last ‌week.

Its shares listed at ₹131 ‌on the National ⁠Stock Exchange, ‌compared with an issue price of ‌₹97 per share.

The rupee rose marginally by 1 paisa to 95.73 on Wednesday, assisted by RBI intervention, as heightened tensions in West Asia kept global markets on the edge.

Crude oil futures traded higher on Wednesday morning as there was no sign that the standoff between the US and Iran over reopening the Strait of Hormuz would end soon. The Strait of Hormuz is a vital link for global crude oil shipping.

Crude oil futures traded higher on Wednesday morning as there was no sign that the standoff between the US and Iran over reopening the Strait of Hormuz would end soon. The Strait of Hormuz is a vital link for global crude oil shipping. At 9.38 am on Wednesday, October Brent oil futures were at $91.65, up by 0.69 per cent, and October crude oil futures on WTI (West Texas Intermediate) were at $84.77, up by 0.84 per cent. August crude oil futures were trading at ₹8194 on Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX) during the initial hour of trading on Wednesday against the previous close of ₹8143, up by 0.63 per cent, and September futures were trading at ₹8135 against the previous close of ₹8088, up by 0.58 per cent.

Bitcoin traded near $64,350 on Wednesday morning, up roughly 0.3% over 24 hours, after moving between approximately $64,005 and $64,926. Immediate support is around $64,000, followed by the more important $63,000 zone. Resistance lies at $64,900-$65,000, followed by $66,000. The short-term holder cost basis near $68,700 remains the larger recovery hurdle.

On-chain indicators continue to suggest caution. Bitcoin’s spot liquidity remains weak and on-chain activity subdued, even as capital flows show signs of stabilising. Spot volume has recently fallen to its lowest level since 2019, while $63,000 represents the Median Realised Price. This suggests selling pressure may be easing, but stronger demand is still required for a sustained breakout.

Institutional flows have improved. US spot Bitcoin ETFs attracted $865.3 million between August 3 and 7, before recording approximately $385.2 million in net outflows from August 10-14. Flows reversed sharply with $297.5 million of inflows on August 17 and another $45.7 million on August 18.

Large-cap altcoins were modestly positive. Ethereum traded near $1,911 (+0.5%), BNB around $603 (-0.1%), XRP near $0.998 (+0.2%), Solana at $76.70 (+1.3%), and TRON around $0.3325 (+0.5%).

Macro conditions remain decisive. A Reuters survey found that 94 of 104 economists expect the Fed to keep rates unchanged at 3.50%-3.75% in September. Markets are also pricing in close to a 70% probability of a hold. Fed minutes due today will be closely watched, followed by July PCE inflation ahead of the September 15-16 meeting. Elevated oil prices and Middle East tensions remain an inflation risk.

Our advice: Bitcoin remains range-bound. A sustained move above $65,000-$66,000, accompanied by stronger spot activity and continued ETF inflows, would provide a more convincing signal that the recovery is broadening.

Markets opened flat to marginally negative on Wednesday, extending a six-session losing streak, as rising crude oil prices and surging global bond yields kept investor sentiment under pressure.

Adani Enterprises Ltd., the flagship of Asia’s richest man Gautam Adani, is back to where it stood just before the conglomerate’s crisis began more than three years ago: the best-performing stock on India’s equity benchmark.
